main_text.p: dem recte foveant, (quod certissime præstituri sunt) præsertim cum ad manum sint quæcunque fovere, & longissime absint quæ flammæ huic, si semel in incendium erumpat, restinguendæ conducere possent; & quod multo peßimum est, cum satis appareat exstingui non posse sine insigni victoris damno.

Præterea licet merito suspicari possemus, convocatione hac vestri parlamenti, quæ eorum consiliis suggesta fuit qui malum hoc civilis discordiæ in clarissima hac insula sine vestro consensu aut consilio excitarunt, intendi, ut oleum potius quam aquam restinguendæ huic flammæ afferatis, & in motuum horum fervore vobis auxiliatoribus utantur ad constantissimorum vestrorum amicorum ruinam procurandam; quos illi interim ut hostes suos ulciscentur. Nihilominus tamen bonis omnibus in celeberrimo vestro coetu non ingratum futurum speramus, quod summo animi gaudio & hilaritate profitemur ac declaremus, vincula amoris & fraternæ charitatis inter nos esse mutua, & sibi invicem in omnibus erga Deum & hominem, principem & populum officiis usque adeo arcte conjuncta, ut communes amicos & inimicos necesse sit habeamus, seu promiscuam utrique salutem contra hostes exteros defendendo, seu alterutrius privilegia contra domesticos subversores tuendo, a quibus maius imminet periculum: nisi ab unica & firma salutis nostræ regula animus nobis fit defcisccre.

Nam cum ratione situs huius insulæ & unionis sub uno capite, omnes tanquam in una eademque domo simus, qua corruente, in ejusdem ruinis promiscue omnes sepeliemur: omnes tanquam in una eademque navi vehamur, qua naufragium patiente aut ad infames divisionis scopulos impingente, vix enatabimus; Æquis animis feratis, quod tempestate adhuc

page.notes: Page is a continuous text page. Running head read as "HISTORIA MOTUUM" (printed as "Historia motuum" in small capitals). Two places are doubtful: "constantissimorum" in the line "ruinam procurandam" is printed "constantissimorum" and "vestrorum amicorum" is a plausible reading; the word "fit defcisccre" near the end of the second paragraph is doubtful, and "unionis" in the third paragraph is read as printed. Several words in the first paragraph are only partly legible due to the scan's gutter shadow on the left edge; "dem" at the start is a fragment of "eadem" cut by the page top. Lines of the third paragraph's last line ("te adhuc") are shown as printed. The printed text reads "motuum" in the running head and body, not expanded.
